display_name: Glengoyne 24 Year Old White Oak (Oak Masters' Series)
cask: American first-fill bourbon + virgin/new (white) oak. NOTE: distinct from the 25 Sherry Oak — the 24 White Oak is bourbon/virgin-oak matured (vanilla/citrus profile), NOT sherry. Debut release of the Oak Masters' Series.
outturn_or_availability: Limited release ('will not return once sold out'). UK launch 10 Jul 2024 (RRP £430); US debut Mar 2025 ($400). Exact outturn N/A — not found.

tasting.nose: Rich vanilla and toasted oak, lemon curd, honey, plum jam, desiccated coconut, spiced apple pastry dusted with icing sugar and lime zest; per Whisky Advocate also passion-fruit panna cotta, dried mango and cinnamon spice.
tasting.palate: Gently balanced and bright: lemon and key-lime pie, honeycomb, gentle tropical notes and soft oak, with star anise, vanilla and emerging chocolate (Whisky Advocate finds rich chocolate ganache/cocoa); Drinkhacker notes white chocolate, grapefruit pith and big toasty charred oak.
tasting.finish: Long and well-aged: toffee apple, delicate citrus and lingering oak, with chocolate sticking the landing.
tasting.narrative: Glengoyne's deliberate 'new flavour direction' — the same slow-distilled Highland spirit pushed away from sherry into first-fill bourbon and virgin oak. Where the 25 trades on dried fruit and chocolate, the 24 White Oak is bright and dessert-like: vanilla, lemon/lime, honey and coconut over a charred-oak spine, with cocoa arriving late. Critics rate it highly (Robb Report's #2 whisky of 2025; Drinkhacker A-), though Drinkhacker hints the spirit is 'just now cresting into over-maturity.' Curator verdict: a strong, citrus-and-vanilla counterpoint to the sherried core range — keep its profile firmly separate from the 25 Sherry Oak.

scores.raw: #2 whisky released in 2025 (Best of the Best 2025)
